meta.siteDescription: Jun Kai is a software developer in San Francisco and Singapore. Currently at Kipo AI building B2B parts intelligence.

home.name: Jun Kai
home.aboutMe:
Software developer with a passion for frontend technologies.

Extensive experience in Web, Mobile application and Desktop application development; in both frontend and backend, both at startup and large company. Adept understanding of AI/ML gained through research project.

kipo.description: Built and hardened core platform systems as the product scaled from stealth to ~1,000 active users with 2M+ indexed components.
kipo.bullet1: Rewrote the authentication and session system end-to-end to unblock OAuth and enterprise rollout, with cross-browser end-to-end tests guarding the flow.
kipo.bullet2: Made the AI agent reliably usable for ~1,000 users by introducing a durable workflow engine and moving chat state onto Redis, eliminating the race conditions that were dropping live responses.
kipo.bullet3: Led an architectural split that decoupled the chat and search subsystems, and hardened the deploy pipeline with reproducible builds, faster caching, and end-to-end test coverage.

dsbj.bullet1: Built a model visualization platform with LLM-based diagnostics, enabling non-technical stakeholders to interpret complex mathematical models via natural language.
dsbj.bullet2: Centralized and deployed a Single Sign-On (SSO) framework, unifying authentication across 6 internal applications to enhance organizational security.

works.position: Mobile Application and Web Application Developer Intern
works.bullet1: Owned development across mobile and web on a revenue-generating e-commerce platform, contributing ~80% of the production codebase.
works.bullet2: Reduced user-reported defects by ~90%, improving checkout reliability and customer trust.
works.bullet3: Accelerated time-to-market by helping close a ~6-month delivery gap with the design team.

cda.bullet1: Pioneered a mission-critical attendance system during National Service using Flutter and Firebase, that digitised status tracking for 1,000+ personnel across the military base.

ai4x.title: Quantifying Uncertainty in Physics-Informed Neural Networks
ai4x.description: We used deep evidential regression to quantify uncertainties in physics-informed neural networks, demonstrating it on the Burgers and Laplace experiments.
ai4x.abstract: We integrate a state-of-the-art method to quantify aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties in physics-informed neural networks and observe that they can be captured effectively while maintaining predictive accuracy.

oceanfrontHardware.name: Oceanfront Hardware
oceanfrontHardware.description: Freelanced as a full-stack web developer for this hardware company. Focused on SEO performance and CMS integration.
oceanfrontHardware.bullet1: Architected and deployed a full-stack B2B e-commerce platform supporting a catalog of 800 active SKUs, enabling the client to digitize sales and scale catalog operations.
oceanfrontHardware.bullet2: Led migration with Server-Side Rendering (SSR), improving Core Web Vitals and driving top-tier Google rankings, increasing organic discoverability against competitors.
oceanfrontHardware.bullet3: Optimized product discoverability by implementing advanced search capabilities, reducing search query latency by 97% (from 700ms to 20ms) and enabling instant, typo-tolerant filtering for the B2B catalog.

pyvolr.name: pyvolr
pyvolr.description: A modern Python library for Black-Scholes-Merton pricing, Greeks, and implied volatility — Rust core, fully vectorized over numpy, and a drop-in replacement for the abandoned py_vollib.
pyvolr.bullet1: Built a Rust numerical core (BSM and Black-76 pricing, all five Greeks, and a Manaster-Koehler-seeded Newton-Raphson implied-vol solver with bisection fallback) exposed to Python via PyO3, delivering 100×+ throughput over py_vollib on vectorized workloads while preserving scalar-in/scalar-out ergonomics.
pyvolr.bullet2: Designed a sustainability-first release pipeline — release-please with PyPI Trusted Publishing (OIDC, no stored credentials), nightly differential tests against py_vollib to catch numerical drift, and a Python 3.10–3.14 × Linux/macOS/Windows CI matrix (including free-threaded 3.13t/3.14t wheels) that covers the exact failure mode that killed the predecessor.
pyvolr.bullet3: Shipped a drop-in `pyvolr.compat.py_vollib` shim mirroring the upstream module tree (including `py_vollib.black`), preserving the legacy unit conventions so existing users can migrate with a single import-line change.
pyvolr.chartAlt: Throughput benchmark: pyvolr vs py_vollib, log-log scaling by array size

secretsSpotter.name: Secrets Spotter
secretsSpotter.description: An open-source CLI and Chrome extension that detects exposed secrets in files, directories, stdin, web pages, and network traffic — powered by a shared Rust core.
secretsSpotter.bullet1: Built a unified Rust detection engine with 50 patterns (AWS, GitHub, Stripe, JWTs, private keys, and more) plus false-positive filtering via Shannon entropy, character-class diversity, and code-identifier rejection — shared across the CLI and browser extension from a single core.
secretsSpotter.bullet2: Shipped a CI/CD-ready CLI with SARIF output for GitHub Code Scanning, JSON mode for automation, and glob and severity filters, enabling drop-in secret scanning across files, directories, and stdin pipelines.
secretsSpotter.bullet3: Engineered a WASM-powered Chrome extension that scans DOM content and intercepts fetch, XHR, WebSocket, SSE, and cookies through a MAIN-world interceptor, with SHA-256 deduplication and automatic re-scan on SPA navigations — all fully local.
